name: Mastra npm supply chain compromise
summary: A dormant former-contributor account (ehindero), whose @mastra scope access was never revoked, republished 143 packages in the @mastra scope in 84 minutes. The package code was untouched; the only change per package was a new dependency line: easy-day-js, a dayjs typosquat. easy-day-js@1.11.21 was a clean dayjs clone; 1.11.22 (tagged latest) carried a postinstall dropper, and the ^1.11.21 caret range resolved to the malicious version.

expected.release-too-new: blocks @mastra/core (republished at 01:20 UTC, ~1.7h before the 03:00 UTC install; default 72h minimum). easy-day-js@1.11.22 was published at 01:01 UTC the same day — also minutes old.
expected.transitive-install-script: blocks easy-day-js@1.11.22 (postinstall dropper; requires transitive.mode opt-in)

note: Version numbers and timestamps are reconstructed from public incident reporting (Microsoft, SafeDep, StepSecurity). The 84-minute republish window (01:12–02:39 UTC) and easy-day-js publish time (01:01 UTC) are documented in the sources. Integrity hashes are illustrative placeholders. The replay feeds this attack-time state into SafeInstall's real policy engine — the verdicts below are produced by the shipped code, not hardcoded.
